stem: A 10-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by ambulance after a bicycle crash. He was not wearing a helmet and was knocked unconscious. Which one of the following preventive measures could have significantly influenced this case?

options.text: Reducing the speed limit on residential streets

explanation: Bicycle helmets reduce the risk of head injury and serious traumatic brain injury in children after a bicycle crash, making this the most relevant preventive measure in this case.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: This is a straightforward prevention question linked to paediatric bicycle-related head trauma. The best answer is the measure most strongly associated with reducing head injury severity: helmet wearing.

optionExplanations.A: Lower traffic speeds may reduce injury severity in some settings, but it is less directly applicable than helmet use for preventing head injury here.
optionExplanations.B: Cycle paths may improve cycling safety overall, but they do not specifically protect against head injury as effectively as a helmet.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Helmets significantly reduce the risk and severity of head injury in bicycle crashes.
optionExplanations.D: High-visibility clothing may improve rider visibility to drivers, but it does not prevent impact-related head injury.
optionExplanations.E: Cycling proficiency testing may improve safety awareness, but it is not as directly protective against traumatic brain injury as helmet use.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury
source.questionTextHtml:
On recognition of his extradural haematoma, Johnny is transferred urgently to theatre, where he undergoes neurosurgical intervention to evacuate the haematoma, before transfer to PICU.

In contrast to adult injury patterns, children have a higher incidence of isolated head injury in major trauma. Traumatic brain injury represents a huge proportion, not only of mortality, but also morbidity in paediatric trauma as survivors with long-term neurological impairments present significant social, emotional and financial costs to their families and local healthcare services. Bicycle crashes are the second leading cause of traumatic brain injury in children.

Which one of the following preventive measure could have significantly influenced this case?

Reducing the speed limit on residential streets

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
